One-line fix, one library file. Here's the rundown, human-style:

## Root cause 🐶

In `src/click/utils.py`, `make_default_short_help()` walks the words of the first docstring paragraph, accumulating length. Its sentence-end check was:

```python
if word[-1] == "." and i == last_index:  # only fires on the LAST word
```

That extra `i == last_index` clause meant click only honored a sentence boundary when the period happened to land on the **final word** of the paragraph. For `Initialize the repo. Creates files and directories as needed.`, the first sentence ends at word index 2 (`repo.`) — not the last — so the check was skipped. The loop kept running until it hit `max_length` and got lopped off with `...`, producing `Initialize the repo. Creates files and...`.

## The fix

```python
if word[-1] == ".":  # sentence end, truncate without "..."
    return " ".join(words[: i + 1])
```

Now it returns at the first sentence-ending word, which is exactly what a "short help" is supposed to be. The order of checks is untouched, so:
- **No sentence end** → still falls through to the old `max_length` + `...` truncation (verified: `Some text without any sentence end that is quite long indeed` → `Some text without any sentence end that is...`).
- **Over-long first sentence** → still trims with `...` because the `total_length > max_length` break comes first (verified: `123 567 90123.` with `max_length=10` → `123 567...`).

## Verification ✅

- The pre-existing parametrized tests in `tests/test_utils.py` (which already expected `123 567 9.` for the "sentence < max" case) now pass — 14/14.
- Full suite: **588 passed, 22 skipped, 1 xfailed**, zero failures.
- End-to-end group help now renders `init  Initialize the repo.` instead of the buggy ellipsized version.

Only `src/click/utils.py` was touched — no tests added, edited, or deleted. Also, `last_index` is still used by the sibling check, so no dead code was introduced (YAGNI would've had my head otherwise).
